title: Gel-free sample preparation techniques and bioinformatic enrichment analysis to in depth characterise the cell wall proteome of mycobacteria
author: Hermann, Giddey, et al.
materials: One major hurdle of cell wall proteomics for mycobacteria is sample loss as a consequence of using gel-based sample preparation techniques that are typically required for sufficient detergent removal. We employed gel-free sample preparation procedures that have been developed previously for removal of detergents [15]. For this purpose, a minimum of 50 μg of each cell fraction was transferred into a Ultracel 30,000 MWCO centrifugal unit (Amicon Ultra, Merck) and concentrated by centrifugation at 14,000 × g for 15 min. The samples were washed three times with buffer UA (8 M urea, 0.1 M Tris, pH 8.5), reduced with 100 mM DTT for 30 min at room temperature and excess DTT was removed by centrifugation for 15 min at 14,000 × g. Iodoacetamide (0.05 M, final concentration) was added to each sample and incubated in the dark at room temperature for 20 min. Excess iodoacetamide was removed by three rounds of buffer exchange with UA buffer followed by three rounds of buffer exchange into ABC buffer (0.05 M ammonium bicarbonate pH 8.0, 20 mM CaCl2). Depending on the trypsin used, the addition of 20 mM CaCl2 can optionally be omitted. Sequence-grade Trypsin (NEB) was added to the samples at an enzyme to protein ration of 1:50 – 1:100 and incubated in a wet chamber overnight (at least 18 h). Tryptic peptides were eluted by three rounds of buffer exchange with ABC buffer and desalted using home-made STAGE tips that contain Empore Octadecyl C18 solid-phase extraction disks (Supelco). C18 disks were activated with three washes with solvent B (80% acetonitrile, 0.1% formic acid) and equilibrated with three washes with solvent A (2% acetonitrile, 0.1% formic acid). Tryptic peptides (10 μg) were loaded on the C18 disc and the disc then centrifuged at 4000 × g for 1 min before being washed three times with solvent A. Peptides were then eluted three times with solvent C (60% acetonitrile, 0.1% formic acid) into glass capillary tubes. Eluted peptides were dried under vacuum and resuspended with solvent A to a concentration of 200 ng/μl.

We used standard procedures for LC–MS/MS analysis of the tryptic peptides. Briefly, separation of peptides by liquid chromatography was performed on an Ultimate 3500 RSnano UPLC system (Dionex) using a home- made precolumn (100 μm ID × 20 mm) connected to an analytical column (75 μm × 200 mm) packed with C18 Luna beads (5 μm diameter, 100 Å pore size; Phenomenex 04A-5452). Desalted peptides (200 ng per sample) were loaded onto the column with a starting mobile phase of 2% ACN, 0.1% formic acid and separated at a constant flow rate at 300 nL/min by the following optimised gradient: 10 min at 2% ACN, increase to 6% ACN for 2 min, to 60% ACN over 60 min, to 80% ACN over 5 min, followed by a column wash of 80% for 13 min. Mass spectra were collected on a Q Exactive mass spectrometer (Thermo) in a data-dependent manner with automatically switching between MS and MS/MS scans using a top-10 method. Peptides were ionised by electrospray ionisation and MS spectra were acquired at a resolution of 70,000 with a target value of 3 × 106 ions or a maximum integration time of 250 ms. The scan range was restricted between 300 and 1750 m/z. Peptide fragmentation was performed by higher-energy collision dissociation (HCD) with the energy set at 25 NCE. Intensity threshold for ions selection was fixed at 1.7 × 104 with charge exclusion of z = 1 and z > 5. The MS/MS spectra were acquired at a resolution of 17,500, with a target value of 2 × 105 ions or a maximum integration time of 120 ms and the isolation window was set at 4.0 m/z. The obtained RAW data files were processed with Maxquant version 1.5.3.12 (http://www.biochem.mpg.de/5111795/maxquant) for protein and peptide identification using the Andromeda search engine and the Uniprot proteome for M. smegmatis (Proteome ID: UP000000757, 6601 proteins, 14/05/2016). The normal default parameter settings were used for the MS/MS database search, with carbamidomethylation of cysteine residues and acetylation of the protein N-terminus selected as fixed modifications. Trypsin/P was selected as protease, iBAQ quantitation and the ‘match between runs’ feature were enabled. Reverse hits and common contaminants were removed from the identified protein list. Likewise, only protein identifications with a q-value < 0.01 and two or more unique peptides were retained for the further analysis.

steps.title: Concentrate cell fractions
steps.instruction: Transfer at least 50 μg of each cell fraction into an Ultracel 30 kDa MWCO centrifugal unit (Amicon Ultra, Merck) and centrifuge at 14,000 × g for 15 min to concentrate the sample.

steps.title: Wash and reduce proteins
steps.instruction: Wash the concentrate three times with buffer UA (8 M urea, 0.1 M Tris, pH 8.5). Add 100 mM DTT, incubate 30 min at room temperature, then remove excess DTT by centrifugation at 14,000 × g for 15 min.

steps.title: Alkylate cysteines
steps.instruction: Add iodoacetamide to a final concentration of 0.05 M, incubate in the dark at room temperature for 20 min.

steps.title: Buffer exchange to ABC buffer
steps.instruction: Remove excess iodoacetamide by three rounds of buffer exchange with UA buffer, then perform three rounds of buffer exchange into ABC buffer (0.05 M ammonium bicarbonate, pH 8.0, 20 mM CaCl₂; CaCl₂ can be omitted if desired).

steps.title: Digest proteins with trypsin
steps.instruction: Add sequence‑grade Trypsin (NEB) at an enzyme‑to‑protein ratio of 1:50–1:100, place the unit in a wet chamber and incubate overnight (≥18 h).

steps.title: Elute peptides and C18 cleanup
steps.instruction: Elute tryptic peptides by three rounds of buffer exchange with ABC buffer. Desalt using homemade STAGE tips containing Empore Octadecyl C18 disks (Supelco): activate disks with three washes of solvent B (80 % acetonitrile, 0.1 % formic acid), equilibrate with three washes of solvent A (2 % acetonitrile, 0.1 % formic acid), load 10 μg of peptides, centrifuge at 4,000 × g for 1 min, wash three times with solvent A, elute three times with solvent C (60 % acetonitrile, 0.1 % formic acid) into glass capillary tubes, dry under vacuum and resuspend in solvent A to 200 ng/μL.

steps.title: Prepare LC‑MS/MS run
steps.instruction: Load 200 ng of desalted peptides onto an Ultimate 3500 RSnano UPLC system (Dionex) equipped with a home‑made precolumn (100 μm ID × 20 mm) and an analytical column (75 μm × 200 mm) packed with C18 Luna beads (5 μm, 100 Å, Phenomenex 04A‑5452). Use a starting mobile phase of 2 % ACN, 0.1 % formic acid and a flow rate of 300 nL/min.

steps.title: Acquire mass spectra
steps.instruction: Run the following gradient: 10 min at 2 % ACN, increase to 6 % ACN over 2 min, to 60 % ACN over 60 min, to 80 % ACN over 5 min, then hold at 80 % ACN for 13 min. Acquire data on a Q Exactive (Thermo) using a top‑10 data‑dependent method: MS resolution 70,000, target 3 × 10⁶ ions (max 250 ms), scan 300–1750 m/z; HCD at 25 NCE; intensity threshold 1.7 × 10⁴, exclude charges z = 1 and z > 5; MS/MS resolution 17,500, target 2 × 10⁵ ions (max 120 ms), isolation window 4.0 m/z.

steps.title: Process data with MaxQuant
steps.instruction: Process RAW files with MaxQuant v1.5.3.12 (Andromeda) using the M. smegmatis Uniprot proteome (Proteome ID: UP000000757, 6601 proteins, 14/05/2016). Apply default parameters, set carbamidomethylation of cysteine and N‑terminal acetylation as fixed modifications, select Trypsin/P as protease, enable iBAQ quantification and ‘match between runs’, remove reverse hits and common contaminants, and retain proteins with q‑value < 0.01 and ≥2 unique peptides.

steps.title: Perform in‑silico enrichment analysis
steps.instruction: Upload the MaxQuant output to Perseus v1.5.2.6, filter out reverse hits, contaminants and proteins with q‑value > 0.01, log₂‑transform iBAQ values, and conduct a volcano‑plot analysis comparing the cell‑wall or cell‑debris fraction (test, n ≥ 3) to the cytosolic fraction (reference, n ≥ 3) using the default FDR = 0.05 and S₀ = 0.1. Proteins exceeding these thresholds are considered significantly enriched in the cell‑wall fraction.
